findings.title: _resolve_session_id references settings.memory_enabled but the shown main snippet never threads memory/attach_memory; the attach wiring is prose-only
findings.location: Decision A — agent/chat.py snippet (main / _resolve_session_id) and Files-to-modify agent/chat.py bullet
findings.fix: Add a sketch of the updated _run_single/_run_repl showing build_agent(memory=settings.memory_enabled, session_id=...), the post-construction 'if result.session_manager is not None: attach_memory(result.agent, result.session_manager)', and the resume/new-session print, so the flag cannot be wired without the attach.

findings.title: 'resuming' vs 'new session' notice has no defined source of truth
findings.location: Decision A and Decision C — the one-line session notice
findings.fix: Define it mechanically without a network call: print 'new session <id>' only when the id was uuid4-generated this run (neither flag nor env supplied it); otherwise 'using session <id>' instead of asserting 'resuming'. Have _resolve_session_id also return whether it generated the id, or expose a sibling predicate.

findings.title: argparse nargs='*' mis-parses a message token beginning with '-'
findings.fix: A prompt starting with '-' errors under argparse though it passes verbatim today. Either document the limitation, use parse_known_args()/'--' handling, or pull --session-id out manually and treat the remainder as the message verbatim (snippet in the review doc).

findings.title: BuildResult.session_manager/mcp_client typed as 'object | None', erasing the surface Task 6 and attach_memory read
findings.fix: Annotate with the real types under a TYPE_CHECKING import (MCPClient, AgentCoreMemorySessionManager) to keep imports offline-safe while carrying intent for .session_id/.initialize/.register_hooks.
